title: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death
hook: in the duel with Arjuna, the earth takes hold of Karna's wheel
tomorrow: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death

segments.voice: Yesterday: Arjuna nearly drew his sword on his own brother, and Krishna asked what truth is for. Your line was the brothers weep, and Yudhishthira blesses him.

Karna and Arjuna, at last, face to face. Karna fits a terrible arrow to his bow, an arrow with a serpent in it, the epic says, a snake with an old grudge against Arjuna. Shalya, at the reins, gives him advice: aim for the chest. Karna refuses. He doesn't aim twice, he says, and he looses at Arjuna's head. And Krishna, driving the other chariot, presses down with his feet, and the chariot sinks into the earth, just enough. The serpent arrow takes Arjuna's crown and leaves Arjuna alive. Hold on to that sinking chariot.
screen: `THE SERPENT ARROW.` → `AIM FOR THE CHEST.` → `KRISHNA PRESSES DOWN.`

segments.voice: The duel goes on, and then the earth takes hold of Karna's chariot wheel. It sinks, and it stays sunk. The chariot lurches and won't move. In the same moment, Karna reaches in memory for his great weapon, and it isn't there. He can't remember the words. The epic explains both with old curses. Long before, Karna had killed a Brahmin's cow by accident, and the Brahmin cursed him: at the moment you most need it, the earth will swallow your wheel. And Karna had once trained under the great teacher Parashurama, hiding that he wasn't a Brahmin. When the teacher found out, he cursed him to forget the weapon he'd learned in the hour he most needed it. Two old debts, the epic says, come due on the same afternoon. Notice the echo. When Krishna pressed his chariot into the earth, the sinking saved Arjuna's life. Now the earth holds Karna's wheel, and the sinking will cost him his. Karna jumps down from the chariot. He grips the wheel with both hands and tries to lift it out of the ground: the commander of the Kaurava army, on foot, straining at a wheel.
screen: `THE EARTH HOLDS THE WHEEL` · `THE WEAPON FORGOTTEN` · `TWO OLD CURSES COME DUE` · then, large: `KARNA LIFTS THE WHEEL`

segments.voice: Put both feet flat on the floor and press down gently; feel the ground press back. Let something that feels stuck come to mind, and don't try to lift it yet, just notice where it sits and how heavy it is. If you pray, you can bring what's stuck into your prayer.
Karna. The warrior whose wheel sinks and whose weapon slips from memory, at the moment he needs them most.
Your line: two old curses at once. The earth that saved Arjuna now holds Karna fast. Until tomorrow.
